sub_strands.title: Overview of Foods and Nutrition
learning_outcomes: a) explain the importance of foods and nutrition as an area of study in Home Science
b) identify careers related to foods and nutrition
c) appreciate the role of foods and nutrition in our day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: discuss the importance of foods and nutrition as an area of study in Home Science
use digital and print resources to search for information on various career opportunities related to foods and nutrition
Participate in career talks in Clubs and Societies with peers, design a career wheel and mount it on the classroom wall.
key_inquiry_questions: How can the knowledge of foods and nutrition inform career opportunities?

sub_strands.title: Kitchen Layouts and Equipment
learning_outcomes: a) analyse kitchen layouts in the home
b) describe tools and equipment used in the kitchen
c) care for tools and equipment used in the kitchen
d) appreciate the importance of different layouts, tools and equipment in the kitchen.
learning_experiences: discuss and illustrate kitchen layouts used in the home (L-shaped, U-shaped, Corridor, One wall, Island)
brainstorm on factors to consider when choosing kitchen layouts, tools and equipment
observe pictures or realia to identify and classify kitchen tools and equipment
care for tools and equipment used in the kitchen (use, clean and store), according to their materials (glass, wood, plastic, melamine, metals, earthenware)
improvise kitchen tools and equipment using safe and locally available materials
key_inquiry_questions: How does a good kitchen layout enhance efficiency when working in the kitchen?
How do kitchen tools and equipment enhance effectiveness when working in the kitchen?

sub_strands.title: Food Hygiene and safety
learning_outcomes: a) explain the importance of hygiene and safety when handling food
b) differentiate between food spoilage and poisoning when handling food
c) apply hygiene practices when handling food
d) adopt high hygiene standards when handling food.
learning_experiences: discuss the importance of food hygiene and safety when handling food

use digital and print resources to search for the difference between food spoilage and poisoning (meaning, causes, signs, and prevention) then share findings with peers Note: (causes; chemicals, micro- organisms, poor storage, poor handling of food, pests and insects; signs; change in colour, change in texture, unpleasant smell, undesirable taste)
observe spoilt food and identify signs of spoilage
practise hygiene when handling food.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is food spoilage and poisoning a concern when handling food?
How can we adopt safe habits and proper hygiene when handling food?

sub_strands.title: Hygiene During Puberty
learning_outcomes: a) explain personal hygiene practices during puberty
b) apply personal hygiene practices during puberty
c) appreciate importance of personal hygiene during puberty
learning_experiences: review the changes that occur in boys and girls during puberty (Physical, Hormonal and Emotional)
search for information on personal hygiene practices during puberty (boys and girls)
discuss measures for managing menstrual hygiene (grooming, handling dignity kits, discomfort during menstruation)
maintain a log on personal hygiene practices carried out during puberty
key_inquiry_questions: How can we maintain hygiene during puberty?

sub_strands.title: Safety in the Home
learning_outcomes: a) explain causes of accidents and injuries at home
b) describe contents of the First Aid kit
c) carry out First Aid for various injuries at home
d) Appreciate the importance of observing safety measures at home.
learning_experiences: Share experiences on causes of accidents and injuries that occur at home (Include preventive measures)
Search for the information on contents of the First Aid kit and their uses
Simulate First Aid for various injuries at home using an improvised or conventional kit(burns, scalds, cuts and bruises, fractures, fainting, Sprains, drowning, Chocking Suffocation)
safely dispose of used first aid materials
key_inquiry_questions: How can we ensure safety in the home?

sub_strands.title: Housing the Family
learning_outcomes: a) explain reasons for housing the family
b) categorise houses found in the community
c) describe methods of housing the family
d) relate rooms to their functions in the house
e) appreciate room interrelationship when housing the family.
learning_experiences: deliberate on reasons for housing the family
discuss and make or draw models of different types of houses in the community using suitable locally available materials (traditional and modern)
Discuss methods of housing the family (building, buying, renting) factors to consider, advantages and disadvantages
watch video clips or use print resources on functions of different rooms in the house and their interrelationship
illustrate the interrelationship of rooms in the house
key_inquiry_questions: 1. What does housing the family entail?
2. Why is room interrelationship in the house important?

sub_strands.title: Sewing Tools, Equipment and Materials
learning_outcomes: a) classify sewing tools, equipment and materials
b) select sewing tools, equipment and materials
c) use, care for and store different sewing tools, equipment and materials
d) appreciate the use and care of sewing tools, equipment and materials
learning_experiences: Search for information from print and digital media and classify sewing tools, equipment and materials (cutting, marking, sewing, measuring, finishing, storage)
Search, brainstorm and present findings on factors to consider when selecting sewing tools, equipment and materials
Visit shops that sell tools, equipment and materials used for sewing and identify the basic needlework items
Share experiences, search and explore information on the use, care and storage of different sewing tools, equipment and materials
Practice safe use, care and storage of needlework tools and equipment while in a Home science laboratory.
key_inquiry_questions: How would you best maintain sewing tools, equipment and materials?

sub_strands.title: Textile Fibres
learning_outcomes: a) identify sources of textile fibres
b) carry out identification of different textile fibres used for household articles
c) analyse the characteristics of different textile fibres used for household articles
d) examine the use of different textile fibres used in the home
e) appreciate different textile fibres used at home
learning_experiences: search for information on the meaning of terms (such as: textiles, fibres, strand, yarn)

study pictures and charts on classification of textile fibres and draw the classification table - Animal - wool, silk - Plant – cotton, linen - Regenerated - viscose rayon - Synthetic - acrylic, polyester
study charts, pictures or watch video clips, brainstorm on methods of identifying textile fibres. Discuss and present findings in class
carry out the identification processes using microscopic, physical, burning test, chemical test
practice safety when carrying out the identification processes in the home science laboratory
use, care and storage of needlework tools and equipment while in a Home Science laboratory
bring samples of fabrics from home to identify their characteristics (strength, elasticity, durability, absorbency and appearance)
collect textile fibres and mount in a folder (the folder to have name of fibre, sources identification process, uses and characteristics of the fibre)
key_inquiry_questions: How do the different characteristics of fibres affect the use of the fabric?
